user.title: Gree Climate Setup

cloud_add.title: Gree Account
cloud_add.description: Enter the details to connect to your Gree account

local_add.title: Local Discovery
local_add.description:
Devices will be automatically discovered by scanning the available networks.

If you have devices on a different subnet or VLAN, enter one or more networks and/or specific IP addresses to probe via unicast. Inter-VLAN routing and firewall rules must allow UDP port 7000 from Home Assistant to the target subnet.

device_picker.title: Discovered Devices
device_picker.description:
Found {devices_found} Gree device(s). Select the devices you want to configure.

When you look for devices again, this list only shows new devices and devices with a new local or cloud connection. Devices you do not select stay as they are. To remove a device, use Remove devices in the menu.

connection_options.title: Connection Options {device_idx} of {device_cnt}

data_description.encryption_key: If left empty will be automatically discovered
data_description.scan_interval: Frequency of the device data polling (in seconds)
data_description.uid: The user ID number that owns the device. Can be 0 if not known

data.mac_controller_local: MAC of the local controller device (discovered: {discovered_mac_local})

data_description.max_online_attempts: The number of attempts to communicate with the device before it is marked as unavailable
data_description.timeout: The timeout for each of the connection attempts

data.mac_controller_cloud: MAC of the cloud controller device (discovered: {discovered_mac_cloud})

data_description.prefer_cloud: Devices prefer local connections. Check if you prefer this device to connect through the cloud

device_options.title: Device Features {device_idx} of {device_cnt}
device_options.description:
The Gree API doesn't have a reliable method of getting the supported features of a device. Please use the options bellow to the best of your knowledge about your device:

 {device_name}

data_description.external_temperature_sensor: If set will replace the built-in HVAC temperature sensor for the Climate entity data
data_description.external_humidity_sensor: If set will replace the built-in HVAC humidity sensor for the Climate entity data
data_description.restore_states: If checked, when the integration is started the device will be overridden by previous states of the integration instead of using the current device state.
data_description.target_temp_step: Sets the increment step for adjusting the target temperature. Fahrenheit degrees are clamped to the nearest integer.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure Devices
reconfigure.description: This entry has {device_cnt} device(s). Pick what to do. Your changes are saved when you choose Save and reload.

rediscover.title: Look for Devices Again
rediscover.description:
This logs in to your Gree account to find its devices. The login logs the Gree app out.

You are reconfiguring a entry with a cloud account. Do you want to look for local devices that match your cloud devices?

edit_device.title: Edit a Device
edit_device.description: Pick the device to edit. If you do not change how it connects, the integration uses the running connection and does not log in to the Gree account.

no_new_devices.title: No New Devices
no_new_devices.description:
No new devices or new connections were found. The IP addresses of the devices that were found are updated.

Submit to go back to the menu. Your changes are saved when you choose Save and reload.

remove_devices.title: Remove Devices
remove_devices.description: Pick the devices to remove from this entry.

legacy_yaml.title: Update your Gree configuration from 4.x
legacy_yaml.description:
Some Gree devices still come from the configuration of Gree 4.x: the `gree:` block in `configuration.yaml`, or devices you set up in the 4.x UI while a YAML block manages the local devices. This version converts them at every start, so they keep working. This legacy import will be removed in a later version.

Comment out the `gree:` block, and keep it in case you want to go back to 4.x. Then paste the block below. If you already have a `gree_custom:` block, add the devices below under its `devices:` instead. Then restart Home Assistant. This message goes away when no device depends on the 4.x configuration any more.

```yaml
{yaml}
```

legacy_folder.title: Remove the old Gree 4.x files
legacy_folder.description:
The folder `custom_components/gree` from Gree 4.x is still installed. HACS does not remove it when it installs this version. The devices of Gree 4.x are moved to this integration, and the old 4.x config entries are disabled.

Delete the folder `custom_components/gree` and restart Home Assistant. The old config entries stay disabled, so you can go back to 4.x. A separate repair lets you remove them.

legacy_entries.title: Remove the old Gree 4.x config entries

confirm.title: Remove the old Gree 4.x config entries
confirm.description:
Your devices now run on this integration. The old config entries of Gree 4.x are kept, disabled, so you can go back to 4.x without setting it up again.

Select **Remove** to remove these old entries. After that, going back to 4.x means setting it up again.
